sekcje: Drug Levels and Effects > Summary of Use during Lactation

Minimal information available on the clinical use of lanadelumab during breastfeeding indicated no infant harm. Because lanadelumab is a large protein molecule with a molecular weight of about 146,000 Da, the amount in milk is likely to be very low. It is also likely to be partially destroyed in the infant's gastrointestinal tract and absorption by the infant is probably minimal. If lanadelumab is required by the mother, it is not a reason to discontinue breastfeeding. Waiting for at least 2 weeks postpartum to resume therapy may minimize transfer to the infant.

Drug Levels and Effects > Effects in Breastfed Infants

An infant was breastfed (extent and duration not stated) by a mother with hereditary angioedema who was using lanadelumab every 3 weeks subcutaneously with no complications. At the age of 2 years, the child was diagnosed with hereditary angioedema but was otherwise healthy.
